app.name: Receipts
preview.title: Preview mode
preview.body: You are looking at the interface outside Anna, so nothing here has been checked against a real CV. Install Receipts to run a real match.
onboarding.heading: Match your CV to any job, without making things up.
onboarding.body: Paste a job posting and Receipts checks every requirement against your real CV, shows you the evidence, then writes bullets and a cover letter using only what you can prove.
onboarding.point1: Every requirement shows the CV line that backs it.
onboarding.point2: Gaps are named plainly, so you can prepare for them.
onboarding.point3: Anything your CV cannot prove never gets written.
cv.add.heading: Add your CV
cv.add.body: Upload a PDF or DOCX, or paste the text. It is saved in your Anna storage and never leaves your account.
cv.add.dropHint: Drop a file here, or choose one. 2 MB maximum.
cv.add.pastePlaceholder: Paste the whole CV, including dates and employers.
cv.preview.heading: Check how we read your CV
cv.preview.body: Every line gets a number. Matches cite these numbers, so a misread line is worth fixing now.
cv.export.done: Saved. {count} lines, word for word as they are here.
cv.export.doneAdditions: Saved. {count} line(s) you added, ready to paste into your own CV.
cv.export.note: Plain text, the way an ATS reads it — your original layout is not kept. Nothing in it was rewritten.
cv.preview.audit: Check what it can't back up
profile.heading: Your profile
profile.body: A headline and an About section, written from your CV and nothing else. No posting is involved, so nothing here can borrow a word from one — every term comes from a line you can point at.
profile.noHeadline: No headline this time: nothing short enough stood up to your CV. The About section below did — and a headline you cannot back is the worst place to start.
cv.profiles.label: Your CVs
cv.profiles.heading: Your CVs
cv.profiles.addBody: This one sits beside the CV you already have. Each CV keeps its own applications, so switching between them switches what you see.
cv.profiles.note: Switching your CV switches the applications you see.
cv.profiles.why: Keep a second CV for a different kind of role. Each one keeps its own applications.
cv.profiles.deleteBody: The CV and the {count} applications checked against it go with it. It can't be undone.
cv.warning.multi_column_suspected: This looks like a two-column layout, so lines may be out of order. Check them, or paste the text instead.
cv.warning.tables_flattened: Tables were flattened into single lines.
cv.warning.truncated: Your CV was long, so the end was left out of the match.
match.new.heading: Paste a job posting
match.new.body: The whole posting works best — requirements, responsibilities, the lot.
match.new.urlLabel: Or paste a link to the posting
match.new.needCv: Add your CV first — a match needs something to check against.
progress.stage.match: Looking for evidence in your CV
map.missingNote: These are worth preparing for, not hiding.
map.noPosting: This match has no saved posting title.
gaps.heading: What your CV doesn't prove yet
gaps.body: Receipts won't write experience you didn't have. So it asks instead — your answer goes into your CV in your own words, and the next match can cite it.
gaps.none: This posting asks for nothing your CV cannot already prove.
gaps.answerPlaceholder: A sentence or two, the way you would say it out loud.
gaps.answerNote: Stored exactly as you type it. Nothing here is rewritten.
gaps.rerun: Your CV has new lines, so this match is now out of date. Run it again to see what they prove.
brief.heading: Before the interview
brief.body: For your {role} application. Every sentence here is one you already have: a line from your CV, or something you sent them.
brief.noMatch: Open an application first. The brief is built from its match, your CV and what you sent.
brief.empty: This match has no requirements, so there is nothing to prepare for.
brief.cvChanged: Your CV changed after you sent this. The version they are reading is the older one.
brief.riskCountOne: 1 requirement worth an answer you have thought about.
brief.riskCountMany: {count} requirements worth an answer you have thought about.
brief.provedBody: Walk in ready to tell each of these as a story. The marked line is the receipt underneath it.
brief.looseBody: These sentences back no single requirement, but they went with the application.
brief.takeCv: Download your CV with those lines in it
brief.risk.no_evidence: They asked for this and your CV does not show it. Prepare the nearest thing you have actually done, and say that instead.
brief.risk.listed_not_shown: Your only evidence is your skills list. Be ready to name where you used it and what you did with it.
brief.risk.self_added: This rests on a line you added here, not on the document you sent. Assume they have not read it.
brief.risk.related_only: Related, not the same thing. Expect a question about the difference.
audit.heading: What your CV can't back up
audit.body: No job posting needed. This reads your CV against itself and shows what an interviewer is most likely to press on.
audit.clean: Nothing in your CV claims more than it shows.
audit.kind.skill_unevidenced: Your skills list names {subject}, but no job, project or certification shows you using it.
audit.kind.title_unevidenced: The top of your CV says {subject}, but none of the roles below carry it.
audit.ask.skill_unevidenced: Where did you use it? One line about the work is enough to back the claim.
audit.ask.title_unevidenced: Which role was it? Name the job that carried the title.
audit.ask.date_conflict: If that's right, be ready to explain it. If it's a typo, fix the line.
audit.answerPlaceholder: One line: what you built or ran, and where.
audit.answerNote: Added to your CV exactly as you type it.
tailor.heading: Suggested bullets
tailor.body: Each suggestion rewrites one of your lines. The source line is always shown, so you can see exactly what changed.
tailor.dropped: We couldn't strengthen this line without adding facts that aren't in your CV.
tailor.empty: No line in your CV needed rewriting for this posting.
letter.heading: Cover letter
letter.body: Every paragraph lists the CV lines it stands on.
export.unverified: {count} line(s) you edited could not be traced back to your CV. The document says so too — check them before you send it.
tracker.heading: Matches
tracker.empty: Your matches will appear here. Paste a job posting to start.
tracker.deleteConfirmBody: The match, its bullets and its letter go with it. Running it again means another analysis.
recurring.heading: What keeps coming up
recurring.body: Across every application you have run, these are the requirements your CV could not prove. Answer one here and it counts in every match from now on.
recurring.asked: Asked in {count} applications, and proved in none of them.
recurring.tooFew: You have run {count} so far. This screen starts saying something useful at {needed}.
recurring.strengthsBody: Asked more than once, and your CV backed it every time.
recurring.noMatches: Run a few matches first. This screen compares them.
recurring.none: Nothing came up more than once across your last {count} applications.
recurring.showWordings: See how the postings worded it
recurring.answerPlaceholder: One line: what you did, and where.
recurring.answerNote: Added to your CV exactly as you type it. Run a match again to see it cited.
ledger.heading: Which lines do the work
ledger.body: Your CV, read back through the applications you have already sent. No model runs here — every number is a citation one of your matches already made, and you can open the application it came from.
ledger.running: Counting what your lines have carried…
ledger.noMatches: Run a match first. This screen counts the citations your applications made.
ledger.tooFew: You have run {count} so far. This screen starts saying something useful at {needed}.
ledger.read: {cited} of your {total} lines have been evidence for something, across {count} applications.
ledger.skipped: {count} application(s) were checked against a different version of this CV. The same line numbers mean different sentences there, so they are left out.
ledger.noneCited: None of these applications cited a line from this CV. Run one again and the citations will land here.
ledger.workingBody: Ranked by how many of your applications cited them. This is the order a reader should meet them in.
ledger.decisiveOne: Once it was the only line behind a must-have. That application rested on this sentence.
ledger.decisiveMany: {count} times it was the only line behind a must-have. Those applications rested on this sentence.
ledger.idleBody: No posting you applied to needed these. That is a fact about the jobs you picked, not about the work — but if the page is a line too long, this is where to look first.
ledger.addedBody: You wrote these here, answering a gap. This is what they have proved since.
ledger.addedProvedOne: Evidence in 1 application since you added it.
ledger.addedProved: Evidence in {count} applications since you added it.
ledger.addedIdle: Nothing has asked for it yet.
since.heading: Since you applied
since.body: For your {role} application. Nothing here is generated — it is the verdicts this application recorded, and the dates on the lines you have written since.
since.noMatch: Open an application first. This screen is about one application and what has moved under it.
since.sentDay: You marked this sent 1 day ago.
since.sentDays: You marked this sent {count} days ago.
since.checkedToday: You ran this match today. Mark it sent on the tracker and this screen can count from that day instead.
since.checkedDay: You ran this match 1 day ago.
since.checkedDays: You ran this match {count} days ago.
since.nothing: Nothing has changed since this went out. When you answer a gap question, an audit finding or a recurring gap, what you write lands here.
since.nothingRelevant: You have added {count} line(s) since this went out, and none of them names anything this posting asked for.
since.worthBody: This posting asked for these, your application could not show them, and your CV has since gained a line that names them. Naming is not proving — only a new match can say what they are worth.
since.runAgainUrl: Opens New match with this posting's link filled in.
since.runAgainPaste: Receipts does not keep the posting's text, so you will need to paste it again.
changed.heading: What changed
changed.body: Two runs of your {role} application, lined up. Nothing here is generated — it is the two verdicts this posting already got.
changed.bodyDays: Two runs of your {role} application, {count} days apart. Nothing here is generated — it is the two verdicts this posting already got.
changed.noEarlier: This posting has only been run once. Run it again after you add something to your CV, and this screen will say what moved.
changed.read: You now have evidence for {after} of {afterTotal}. Last time it was {before} of {beforeTotal}.
changed.wroteOne: You wrote 1 line into your CV between the two runs.
changed.wrote: You wrote {count} lines into your CV between the two runs.
changed.nothing: Nothing moved between these two runs.
changed.lostBody: A posting read twice is not read identically. These had evidence last time and do not now — open both match maps before you trust either.
changed.stillBody: Asked in both runs, and evidenced in neither.
changed.differedBody: These were worded differently in the two runs, so they could not be lined up. Each shows the verdict its own run gave.
changed.onlyNow: Only this run asks for it. Now: {after}.
changed.onlyThen: Only the earlier run asked for it. Then: {before}.
changed.credited: Because of a line you added between the two runs.
map.ranBefore: You have run this posting before.
worth.heading: Worth another look
worth.body: Every application you have saved, asked one question: has your CV gained a line since you sent it that names something it could not show? No model runs here.
worth.noMatches: Nothing saved yet. Run a match, and the applications your later answers would change will land here.
worth.nothingWritten: You have not written anything into your CV yet. When you answer a gap question, an audit finding or a recurring gap, the applications it would change appear here.
worth.none: None of your {count} applications has anything new to go on. That changes the next time you answer a gap.
worth.readOne: 1 of your {total} applications is worth running again.
worth.read: {count} of your {total} applications are worth running again.
worth.of: That is {count} of the {total} things this application could not show.
worth.mustOne: One of them was a must-have.
worth.fromYourLines: from lines you added after you applied
followup.heading: Follow up
followup.body: For your {role} application. The note is built from the lines you have written since you applied — and when there are none, Receipts says so instead of writing one.
followup.running: Reading what you have added since…
followup.noMatch: Open an application first. A follow-up is about one application that has already gone out.
followup.sentDay: You marked this sent 1 day ago.
followup.sentDays: You marked this sent {count} days ago.
followup.checkedToday: You ran this match today. Mark it sent on the tracker and this counts from that day instead.
followup.checkedDay: You ran this match 1 day ago.
followup.checkedDays: You ran this match {count} days ago.
followup.nothingNew: Nothing has changed since you sent this, so there is nothing here worth a stranger's minute. Answer a gap in your own words and this becomes a note worth sending.
followup.standsOn: Written from what you have added since: {list}.
followup.builtOn: Stands on the lines you added after you applied:
compare.heading: Which one you can prove
compare.body: Pick the applications you are choosing between. Receipts lines them up against the verdicts it already recorded — no new analysis, and nothing here calls the model.
compare.pickHint: Two to {max}. The two most recent are picked to start.
compare.needMatches: Run two matches first. This screen compares them.
compare.edgeLabel: Proved here, and the others don't ask for it
compare.sharedGapsHeading: What all of them ask for and none of them prove
compare.sharedGapsBody: One answer here counts in every application on this screen.
compare.sharedProvedHeading: What all of them ask for and you can prove
compare.ordering: Ordered by what your CV can prove. That is not the same as which job you want.
settings.heading: Your data
settings.body: Your CV and every match are stored in your Anna account. Receipts uses no external services.
settings.deleteConfirmBody: This deletes your CV and all matches from Anna. It can't be undone.
summary.sentence: {evidenced} of {total} requirements have evidence in your CV.
common.exampleNote: This is a recorded example. Add your CV to run a real match.
error.file_too_large: This file is over 2 MB. Export a smaller PDF or paste the text.
error.unreadable_file: We couldn't read text from this file. It may be a scanned image. Paste the text instead.
error.cv_too_short: This CV looks too short to match against. Add your experience and try again.
error.no_requirements_found: This text doesn't look like a job posting. Paste the full posting, including requirements.
error.model_output_invalid: The analysis didn't finish cleanly. Run it again — your inputs are saved.
error.sampling_unavailable: Anna couldn't run the model right now. Check your credits or try again in a minute.
error.upload_expired: The upload timed out. Choose the file again.
error.invalid_args: Something about that request didn't line up. Run the match again.
error.rate_limited: That is a lot of runs in a short time. Wait a moment, then run it again.
error.internal_error: The engine hit an unexpected problem. Run it again.
error.host_unavailable: Anna couldn't reach the Receipts engine. Check that your Anna Agent is online.
error.url_fetch_failed: This page didn't let us read it. Paste the posting text instead.
error.save_failed: The match finished but Anna couldn't save it. It is on screen — copy what you need before you close the window.
error.export_failed: The file didn't reach your downloads. Export it again.
error.export_empty: Accept a bullet or write a letter first — there is nothing to put in the document yet.
error.cv_changed: Your CV changed after this match was made. Run the match again before tailoring it.
check.heading: Check a document before you send it
check.body: Paste a CV or cover letter you are about to send — one you wrote yourself, or one another tool wrote for you. Receipts reads every sentence against your CV and shows what it can't back up.
check.pasteLabel: The document you are about to send
check.pastePlaceholder: Paste the whole thing, including dates, numbers and employers.
check.privacy: Nothing you paste here is saved. It is read once and dropped when you leave.
check.forPosting: Written for {posting}, so its name and title are not read as claims.
check.clean: All {checked} sentences trace back to your CV.
check.cleanNote: Nothing in this document claims more than your CV can show.
check.countOne: 1 sentence of {checked} claims something your CV can't back up.
check.countMany: {count} sentences of {checked} claim something your CV can't back up.
check.maskedNote: Not read as claims: {terms}. That is who the document is addressed to, not what it says about you.
check.truncated: This document was long, so the end wasn't read.
check.answerPlaceholder: One line: what you did, and where.
check.answerNote: Added to your CV exactly as you type it. If it didn't happen, take the sentence out of your document instead.
check.saved: Added to your CV. This sentence is backed now.
answers.heading: Answer what the form asked
answers.body: Paste the free-text questions from the application form, or the ones a recruiter emailed. Receipts answers only from what your CV can prove, and tells you plainly when it can't.
answers.pastePlaceholder: Paste the questions, one per line.
answers.capped: {count} at a time. Answer these, then paste the rest.
answers.note: Every sentence cites the CV line behind it. Anything that can't be traced there is dropped, not softened.
answers.droppedOne: 1 sentence was dropped: your CV couldn't back it.
answers.droppedMany: {count} sentences were dropped: your CV couldn't back them.
answers.notAboutYou: This one is yours to answer. Your CV records what you did, not what you want — so there is nothing here to draw on, and Receipts won't write it for you.
answers.noEvidence: Your CV doesn't show anything that answers this. Rather than write around it, here is the question back.
answers.answerPlaceholder: One line: what you did, and where.
answers.answerNote: Added to your CV exactly as you type it, then the questions are asked again.
map.assertPicking: Pick the lines on your CV
map.assertAsk: Which lines on your CV cover “{requirement}”?
map.assertNote: Tap the lines that show it. They stay your call — Receipts records that you said so, and never says it checked.
map.assertedNote: You said these lines cover it. Receipts didn't find it — so this one is yours to make.
map.assertedCountOne: You marked 1 more as covered. That one is your call, not ours.
map.assertedCountMany: You marked {count} more as covered. Those are your call, not ours.
brief.risk.self_asserted: You told Receipts a line covers this and Receipts couldn't see it. Nobody but you has agreed with that yet, so be ready to make the case out loud.
map.unshownOne: The posting asks for {term} by name, and the line below doesn't show it — so this is marked related, not evidenced.
map.unshownMany: The posting asks for {terms} by name, and the lines below don't show them — so this is marked related, not evidenced.
share.heading: Make a receipt you can show
share.body: A picture of this match with nothing of yours in it — no CV lines, no employer, no company. Just the shape: what your CV proved, and what it didn't.
share.sentence: {evidenced} of {total} requirements have evidence in my CV.
share.tagline: Receipts on Anna — tailor every application, invent nothing.
share.roleNote: The only thing on this card that could say which job you are applying for. Off until you say otherwise.
share.contains: On the card: {count} requirements as shapes, and the counts. No lines from your CV, no employer, no wording from the posting.
share.saved: Saved. It is an SVG — any browser opens it, and it scales without going soft.
